assignments.title: Preferences and consumer choice

canonical_specification.outcome: Derive demands and identify corner solutions under a budget constraint.

assignments.content: Define complete/transitive preferences and ordinal utility with strictly increasing transformations; explain continuity/convexity/strict convexity/local nonsatiation without claiming universal utility representation. Positive-price budget sets and existence; Marshallian demand as correspondence versus unique function, homogeneity/budget exhaustion under stated assumptions; derive interior and corner cases with full economic interpretation; indifference curves/MRS conventions and revealed preference with precise WARP logic and falsification limits. At least two full worked examples (one smooth interior, one genuine corner/kink) and eight fully solved exercises including transfer/proof/critique. Link the foundation assessment and earlier mathematical prerequisites; successor c02. Use n-good notation p,x,m then transparent two-good calculations. Do not preempt full compensated demand/Slutsky/welfare derivation in c02.
assignments.state: accepted by root in prerequisite order

assignments.title: Demand, duality and welfare

canonical_specification.outcome: Decompose price responses and measure welfare with correct income concepts.

assignments.content: Assume c01 teaches ordinal preferences, budget choice and Marshallian demand. Define indirect utility v(p,m), expenditure e(p,u), Hicksian correspondence h(p,u), and conditions for dual identities, attainment and differentiability. Derive Shephard and Roy with stated regularity; derive Slutsky by differentiating x(p,e(p,u))=h(p,u), substitution negative semidefinite/symmetry from concavity, normal/inferior/Giffen distinctions. Define CV/EV with explicit sign and baseline/target utility conventions, derive exact numerical price-change welfare and compare consumer-surplus approximation/quasilinear case. At least two fully worked original examples and eight complete exercise solutions including a boundary/nondifferentiability case, proof/derivation, transfer and welfare critique. All notation and methods taught before exercises; leave graduate general proofs/extensions to Volume13 without falsely claiming them supplied.
assignments.state: accepted by root in prerequisite order

assignments.title: Production, costs and firm choice

canonical_specification.outcome: Derive cost functions and output/input choices from technology.

assignments.content: Assume c01/c02 basic constrained choice and expenditure duality. Define technology/production sets, inputs/output/time units, free disposal and feasible boundary; distinguish marginal products, diminishing returns and returns to scale. Derive conditional factor demand/cost with an original smooth technology and a corner or fixed-proportions alternative; short-run versus long-run inputs/costs, MC/AC/AVC and envelope conditions; profit-maximizing competitive supply, shutdown/exit, sunk versus avoidable fixed costs and possible correspondences/existence failures. At least two full worked examples and eight fully solved original exercises with all derivations/assumptions, transfer/proof/critique. Explicitly hand off aggregate market clearing, tax incidence and free-entry market equilibrium to c04. Use p output price, w/r input prices, q output, L/K inputs, avoid confusing fixed cost with marginal cost.
assignments.state: accepted by root in prerequisite order

assignments.title: Competitive equilibrium and surplus

canonical_specification.outcome: Solve partial equilibrium and distinguish efficiency from distribution.

assignments.content: Build partial-equilibrium market demand/supply from horizontal aggregation, existence/uniqueness/nontrade boundary conditions, comparative statics and the price-taker premise. Define consumer/producer surplus and exact welfare under quasilinearity/no externalities/efficient rationing; distinguish surplus from profit and distribution/Pareto improvement. Derive tax wedge, local elasticity incidence and finite linear-tax revenue/DWL; explain statutory remittance invariance under assumptions and limitations. Connect entry/exit/minimum long-run average cost to market supply under homogeneous-firm/constant-input-price/free-entry assumptions; show a finite-number caveat and price-control allocation issue. Two full worked examples, eight solved exercises, original exact checks; method-specific sources. Root owns this chapter and all shared integration.
